story:
Seleucus was the general of the legion that marched its emperor west, and when the emperor died at the edge of the world he took the chair. He did not take the dead man's name. The name was struck out, and Seleucus wrote it nowhere, as the law required; whether he made that law or only obeyed it is the whole quarrel of the Cornish scholars.

He governed the legion underground as an emperor governs. He fed it when the ships did not come, gave it halls when the ground was too hard for a city, and wrote a Book of Deeds, plain as the Romans wrote them, so that the reader might judge. In it he set down the oath of his four generals, Olivarius, Taras, Crotus and Amminus, to stand by him in life and after it. They kept it. He sits in the chair still with Taras at his side, and the last leaves of his book, in a shaking hand, ask whoever reads them for release: theirs, and his.

Iohannes Aldar says he is a usurper confessing. Grindan Halig says he is a soldier who obeyed. The minstrels say his name is Greek, and a pretender's. The Spirit of the Emperor, who stands a few paces from his chair, has never once spoken to him.
legend: Emperor Seleucus, level 40, in the emperor's hall of Cardova with Taras, the Forgotten Emperor and the praetorian guards (all Spirits of Rome; clear the guards, they help). The Spirit of the Emperor next to him is peaceful. For Fall of an Emperor he is last: Olivarius, Taras, Crotus, Amminus first, with their foci and the amulet offered, then Seleucus, and loot his book of deeds. Plain melee. Respawns in about five minutes.
